aboutGame.title: What is BAKUDO?
paragraphs: BAKUDO is a sci-fi school ball-sport boss rush action game developed by SAYIL GAMES and published by SHUEISHA GAMES. At Soliris Academy, Yuria has ten in-game days to defeat the Stellar Eight, the school's top-ranked students, while searching for the clue her missing father left behind.

Combat turns ball movement into offense: positioning, return timing, and reading the ball's arc matter as much as reflexes. BAKUDO is planned for Steam and Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027, with a single-player campaign and support for eight languages.

highlights.label: Rally

highlights.label: Chance

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions about BAKUDO.

items.question: What is BAKUDO?
items.answer: BAKUDO is a sci-fi school ball-sport boss rush action game from developer SAYIL GAMES and publisher SHUEISHA GAMES. Yuria enters Soliris Academy's Coreball Department and must defeat the Stellar Eight within ten in-game days while searching for a clue left by her missing father.

items.question: Is BAKUDO a single-player game?
items.answer: Yes. Official materials list BAKUDO as a single-player experience with one player, built around a story-driven academy campaign and a ranked boss-rush ladder.

items.question: When is the BAKUDO release date?
items.answer: BAKUDO is planned for 2027. SHUEISHA GAMES has confirmed the release window but has not announced a specific month or day.

items.question: Which platforms will BAKUDO launch on?
items.answer: BAKUDO is confirmed for Steam and Nintendo Switch 2. The Switch 2 version was revealed during Indie World on October 28, 2026.

items.question: How does BAKUDO combat work?
items.answer: BAKUDO combat is built around Coreball rallies. Positioning, ball-return timing, chance-ball reads, and punishes after telegraphed attacks matter more than mashing; clears are graded, with S Rank as the top benchmark.

items.question: Where can I try the BAKUDO demo?
items.answer: The BAKUDO Boss Rush Demo is available through the official Steam page. Xbox and PlayStation controllers are supported, and replaying one boss is the fastest way to learn its pattern.
